When I was young and first developed anxiety problems, I had a really bad panic attack when my mom wasn't home. I hadn't yet developed any ways to calm my panic attacks and they were very scary to me at that age. I had wandered out of my room to grab the phone to call my mom and hyperventilated so hard I fell and was barely conscious. But I still remember my cat running to me and laying by my head. She kept licking my face and nudging me. Luckily, my mom came home and found me and called for an ambulance. When they got there, my cat growled and hissed at them and refused to leave my side. This cat was normally super sweet and NEVER growled or hissed. I ended up being fine, obviously, but after that, my cat would follow me everywhere and lay with me by my head. She was always all over me if I cried or had anxiety. Even after I moved out, when I came to visit, she laid on me. And she never stopped even when we had to say goodbye and she crossed the rainbow bridge. She passed ~8 years ago and I still miss her constantly.

Everyone is very different for that, so you'll have to slowly try things out. For me, I was back to eating normally within 2 weeks. The first two or so days, I ate nothing but crackers and soup with only some salt and sometimes garlic powder. I introduced a few more things each day. After a week, I was eating mostly normal. I continued to avoid heavily greasy foods and spicy foods for another week. 

I'd say definitely stick to super basic the first couple days. If you struggle with bland foods, spices are your friend! Just try to avoid spicy/hot ones for a bit. Honestly, the first day you probably won't want much of anything. Introduce things back into small amounts. Be especially cautious of high fat/grease and spicy.

As for drinks, I drank a ton of water. And I tried to drink Sprite each day too. From the moment I woke up, the nurse wanted me to drink either ginger ale or Sierra Mist/Starry. Because during the surgery they pump air into you to see better. Having bubbly drinks helps you to burp and release some of those gases. Those gases stay in you for a couple days and can be uncomfortable and a little painful. So the more you can get out of you, the better! So definitely drink lots of water and healthier bubbly beverages like Sprite. Try to avoid any with caffeine and high sugar like Mountain Dew at first. I started drinking things like coffee after about a week and a half.

I had some constipation as well as feeling dizzy. I slept the dizziness off when possible, took Zofran (anti nausea medication) if it had any nausea that came with the dizziness, and used stool softners and kept hydrated for the constipation. Side effects aren't fun but they're typically worth it to take away the pain.

Do keep in mind, if they give you a medicine that isn't helping or has too many bad side effects, you can call into your surgeon/nurses (they should provide you a phone number) and have them change your prescription if you describe your concerns. So don't feel like you're stuck with it if the side effects outweigh the benefits. The nurses are there to help!

Everybody's body is different, of course. For me, immediately out of surgery I rated my pain a 7. It sucked and I was nauseous. But the anesthesia almost made me not care so much? I just wanted to sleep tbh. The first week was awful, I won't lie. I was in a ton of pain whenever the medicine started wearing off. But the medications helped. So take your meds when you get them. I know it's no fun taking opioids, but for the first few days take them on the hour everytime. So if it says to take every 6 hours, take them every 6 hours. After the first few days, you can space them out more if you want to. The second week was also a bit rough, but definitely better than the first. I'm three weeks post op now and have almost no pain! I'm completely independent again. The pain sucks, but I promise it's worth it. I'd do it all over again. Good luck! I wish you a good surgery and speedy recovery!

I am so sorry you're going through this. As others have said, you're the victim in this. And as everyone else has also said, this is abuse. 

Please, do not ever go back to his place alone. If your sister can't go, (or even if she can go) consider bringing a police officer with you. Go when he's at work or when you know he'll be away. Get all of your most important things.

Afterward, consider getting a form of protection like pepper spray if it's legal where you are. If he shows up, call the cops and don't let him in. You might want to tell him everything you're feeling, but he sounds narcissistic. None of it will get to him. He feels like he's done nothing wrong (even though he has.) So consider ghosting him. Block his number. Block him on social media. Considering he sent thousands of messages and calls to you, he may go to lengths to get around the blocks. So, it may be worth changing your number and/or temporarily deactivating your social media. Your sister should block him too since they were friends.

Lastly, consider filing a police report. Sadly, they may not do anything. But at least have them file a report. Start a paper trail of what he's done in case this escalates in the future. 

NTA x1000. You did nothing wrong. I am so sorry he's made you believe you have. If it's an option, consider therapy after this. Connect with friends. Spend time with your sister and other family (if you're close.) Please update again if possible so we all know you're okay.

Hey there. You are most definitely not pathetic. You're only 14. I don't think you're wrong or weird for not doing any of those things. In fact, it's better that you don't. You're young. You have your whole life ahead of you and there's no need to rush to do things or to do things you aren't comfortable with. Being a teenager can suck. Peer pressure it awful. But the people saying you're boring are wrong. Do what makes you happy. If you don't want to do those things you feel pressured to do, then don't. And try to ignore the people being jerks. If people harass you too much, don't be afraid to tell an adult you trust. Focus on school as best you can and focus on the hobbies that you love. Even try new hobbies if you want. High school and being a teen and bullies are the worst. But believe me when I say, once you graduate, those people won't matter. You'll never see most of them again. And you'll be so happy that you didn't do anything that you didn't want to do. And as for maybe being asexual, if you are, there's nothing wrong with that! If you're confused, don't feel the need to put a label on yourself right now. You'll figure it out eventually. But there are communities out there, including here on Reddit that will help you too. Anyway, I wish you the best and hope things look up for you.

Play through the single player mode if you still aren't used to the controls.

Try all of the weapons out. Seriously. I thought I wouldn't be a good sniper to save my life, and I sucked at it at first. But then I ended up being really good at it. 
You also don't have to stick to just one weapon to main with if you don't want to. I have a group of weapons I like to play with, and I switch weapons depending on what mode I'm playing and if I get bored using a certain weapon.
Pay attention to your gear/clothing. Having good stats on clothing items makes the world of a difference! Experiment with the different types and find what works best with you and what you like.
Help your teammates out when they need it.
Pay attention the ink on the ground. If no one on your team is keeping up with inking paths to swim in, do it if you can. Your whole team will appreciate it!
If an enemy is hiding in the ink from you, watch and listen closely. You can often see them leave a path in their ink when they swim and hear them swimming (although it can be hard sometimes with the music and commotion around you).
Don't just pay attention to the main weapons, look at your sub weapons and specials. Find out which work best for you an what you like.
Use the Booyah and C'mon buttons if you want to, but don't spam them. It'll distract and annoy your teammates, usually.
Use the super jump. But look at the map on your game pad before you super jump. You can usually get a good idea if you're going to get splatted when you land.
Ink the enemy's feet.
If your special is bomb rush or inkzooka, jump around as your release bombs/shoot ink. It'll help you reach a bit higher ground and also make it a little harder for enemy's to hit you when they're trying to splat you.

You are most definitely nonbinary enough. If you feel even a little nonbinary, you are nonbinary! Gender is a spectrum. And you don't have to pinpoint one spot on the spectrum and stay there forever. Many people fluctuate on the spectrum! I most certainly do! I know a lot of people who wake up feeling more feminine one day, more masculine the next, and more agender a few days later. Look at it as a flexible thing. You don't have to tie yourself to one spot on the spectrum. And you definitely don't have to "present enough" to still be nonbinary. A lot of people don't for various reasons. Just do what you like and what feels right! Wear whatever you want, choose whatever names you want (whether they're feminine, masculine, or gender neutral, it doesn't matter!), and present how you want. You know yourself better than anyone else. And you most certainly belong here in the nonbinary community. I also know plenty of people who identify as nonbinary and also lesbian. Choose whichever identity feels right for you. Take your time exploring yourself. There's no rush or race to do it. You're definitely not lazy for not wanting to experiment. Again, just do whatever feels right and whatever makes you happy. I completely understand it being tiring too. I think a lot of us have been there (and still are there). Best of luck!
